Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the StellarTech Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Lewis, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Janet Lewis, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to StellarTech’s third quarter earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Hayes, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; and David Lee, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Robert Hayes.

Robert Hayes, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter.

This quarter, we achieved significant progress, including a substantial investment in our long-term growth and operational efficiency with total capital expenditures reaching $6.77 billion. This investment is spread across enhancing our infrastructure, expanding production capacity, and accelerating our digital transformation.

We’re seeing strong revenue performance across all four key growth platforms: Smartphone, High-Performance Computing (HPC), Internet of Things (IoT), and Automotive. Consolidated revenue for Q3 2021 reached NT$435.7 billion, an 11.4% increase compared to Q2 2021.

These results reflect our strategy in action. I’ll now hand it over to Sarah to discuss the financials in more detail.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let’s take a closer look at the numbers.

As Robert mentioned, we saw strong revenue performance this quarter. Consolidated revenue for Q3 2021 reached NT$435.7 billion, an 11.4% increase compared to NT$391.1 billion in Q2 2021. In USD terms, revenue amounted to $15.1 billion, representing a 12% sequential increase from $13.5 billion in Q2 2021. Year-over-year, this represents a 22% increase from the $12.4 billion we reported in Q3 2020. Breaking it down by platform, Smartphone revenue increased by 18% year-over-year to $5.3 billion, HPC surged by 35% year-over-year to $3.8 billion, IoT experienced a healthy 15% year-over-year growth to $3.1 billion, and Automotive witnessed the most impressive growth, increasing by 55% year-over-year to reach $2.9 billion. We previously guided for Q3 revenue between $14.5 billion and $14.8 billion, so we exceeded that guidance by approximately 2%, primarily due to stronger-than-anticipated demand for our HPC solutions. We expect revenue for Q4 2021 to be between $15.4 billion and $15.7 billion, representing a 4.5% sequential increase. Based on this, we expect full-year 2021 revenue to grow approximately 24% year-over-year in USD terms.

Turning to gross margins, in the third quarter, we achieved a gross margin of 51.3%, a 1.3 percentage point increase compared to the second quarter's 50.0% and a 1.5 percentage point increase from Q3 2020's 49.8%. This sequential improvement was driven by enhanced profitability in our back-end manufacturing operations, which contributed 0.9 percentage points, and a shift towards a more favorable technology mix, contributing 0.4 percentage points. The back-end profitability improvement is largely due to the implementation of our automated testing protocol across our Malaysian and Vietnamese facilities, resulting in a 15% reduction in testing time, our Yield Optimization Program which yielded a 12% reduction in scrap rates, and strategic negotiations with packaging material suppliers resulting in a 5% reduction in material costs. The shift in our sales mix towards higher-margin advanced technology products, particularly 5nm chips and our new line of AI accelerator chips, also played a crucial role. The North American market saw the largest demand for these advanced technology products, followed by Europe. In our Q2 earnings call, we guided for a gross margin between 49.5% and 50.5%. Our actual gross margin of 51.3% exceeded the high end of this range by 0.8 percentage points, primarily due to the faster-than-anticipated ramp-up of our 5nm production. Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we expect our gross margin to be between 51% and 53%. This guidance reflects our continued confidence in the strength of our product portfolio, the ongoing improvements in our operational efficiency, and the favorable market dynamics. This implies a full-year 2021 gross margin higher than 50%, a significant improvement compared to 2020's 48.5%.

Regarding capital expenditures, our CapEx for the third quarter totaled $6.77 billion. Approximately $2.8 billion, or 41% of the total, was allocated to expanding our global data center footprint, including bringing online two new hyperscale data centers in Northern Virginia and one in Ireland. $1.9 billion, or 28% of the total, was directed toward upgrading and expanding our manufacturing facilities, primarily focused on our semiconductor division. We allocated $800 million, approximately 12% of the total, to renewable energy projects, including the development of new solar and wind farms, with $350 million dedicated to completing the "Green Horizon" solar farm project in Arizona. The remaining $1.27 billion, or 19% of the total, was invested in digital transformation initiatives and upgrades to our internal IT infrastructure, including upgrading our CRM platform. The largest portion of our CapEx was concentrated in North America, driven by data center expansion and renewable energy projects. We expect CapEx to remain elevated in the coming quarters as we continue to execute on our strategic initiatives.

Now to David, who will cover operational and product updates.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

Let’s revisit capital expenditures from an innovation standpoint.
As Sarah mentioned, we invested $1.9 billion in upgrading and expanding our manufacturing facilities, primarily focused on our semiconductor division. This investment includes the installation of new advanced lithography equipment and the modernization of existing fabrication plants to support the production of next-generation chips. We are seeing particularly strong demand for our high-performance computing (HPC) chips, which are used in AI training and scientific simulations. We anticipate that the investment in expanded manufacturing capacity will begin generating returns in the next 12-18 months.

We launched the Dimensity 3000 series AP, which contributed to 35% of the Smartphone revenue.

We’ve made strong headway with the sales guidance, forecast, or trend by segment next quarter or full year, and expect meaningful results in the first half of next year.
Following a robust Q3, StellarTech anticipates continued sequential growth in Q4, primarily fueled by the surging demand for our industry-leading 5nm process technology. We are projecting a consolidated revenue range of $15.6 billion to $16.0 billion for Q4, representing a sequential increase of approximately 3.5% to 6.1% compared to the Q3 revenue of $15.1 billion. The smartphone segment is expected to remain strong in Q4, growing approximately 4% sequentially, underpinned by robust demand from major smartphone OEMs for their flagship devices utilizing the 5nm process. We project smartphone revenue to contribute approximately 42% to StellarTech's overall revenue in Q4, a slight decrease from 43% in Q3 due to faster growth in other segments. HPC is projected to be the fastest-growing segment in Q4, with an anticipated sequential increase of around 12%, driven by the increasing adoption of 5nm-based CPUs and GPUs in data centers and high-end computing platforms. We forecast HPC to account for approximately 37% of StellarTech's total revenue in Q4, up from 35% in Q3. The IoT segment is expected to experience moderate growth of approximately 2% sequentially in Q4. We project the IoT segment to contribute roughly 8% to StellarTech's Q4 revenue, remaining relatively stable compared to Q3. Despite the global automotive chip shortage, StellarTech's automotive segment is expected to grow by approximately 5% sequentially in Q4. Automotive is expected to contribute approximately 4% to StellarTech's overall Q4 revenue. We project 2022 revenue to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 15%-20% range.

Let’s move to Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
On gross margin, could you expand on the sustainability of the improvements you’ve seen in back-end manufacturing profitability?

Sarah Chen:
Absolutely. We believe these improvements are sustainable. The implementation of our automated testing protocol is now fully rolled out, and we expect to continue to see efficiency gains. Our Yield Optimization Program is an ongoing initiative, and we are constantly working to improve our processes and reduce scrap rates. Finally, we have long-term agreements in place with our packaging material suppliers, so we expect to maintain the cost savings we have achieved.

Analyst 2:
Regarding capital expenditures, what's the scale and outlook for your renewable energy investments?

David Lee:
We’re seeing momentum with our renewable energy investments, especially in the Southwest United States. As Sarah mentioned, we allocated $800 million to renewable energy projects this quarter, including the development of new solar and wind farms. We are committed to achieving carbon neutrality by 2030, and we believe that these investments will not only help us achieve our sustainability goals but also provide long-term cost savings and mitigate potential risks associated with fluctuating energy prices and increasingly stringent environmental regulations.

Closing

Robert Hayes:
Thank you all for joining. We’re proud of our progress and excited for what’s ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
